newsitem.title: UK: Harrisons & Crosfield falls on 97 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Harrisons & Crosfield falls on 97 outlook.

text.p: Shares in Harrisons and Crosfield Plc fell seven pence to 133-1/2, after the conglomerate's 1996 results statement was accompanied by a fairly gloomy outlook for 1997.

While last year's profits met market expectations, investors began to worry over this year's performance after Harrisons warned sterling strength was making itself felt in its food and chemicals businesses, analysts said.

Harrisons, which reported 1996 pretax profits up at 120.8 million stg from 119.6 million stg, said results in the food and agriculture division in the first two months of 1997 were running well behind last year.
The pound's strength also had some adverse impact on the chemicals business, although operating profits here were still ahead in January and February.
Operating profits in the chemicals business rose 12 percent alst year to 55.9 million stg before rationalisation costs. In food and agriculture, profits increased six percent to 33.5 million stg.
Profits in timber and building supplies fell to 15.3 million stg from 21.9 million, but results started to improve in the second half of 1996. This trend continued in the first two months of 1997.
